scorecard.reason: Semantic tokens, density, interaction geometry, themes, RTL-safe composition, and a certified state matrix are kernel-owned; native physical acceptance remains separate.
High-leverage controls, disclosure, progress, media, feedback, identity/status, code, copy, and timeline surfaces are shared; Tooltip remains an explicit recipe/defer boundary.
Production controls, RHF lifecycle, async validation, arrays, server errors, dirty protection, and autosave recipes are shared; universal picker and router interception remain bounded.
Adaptive shell, page/workspace geometry, sticky actions, master/detail, protected routing, overlays, and deep links are sanctioned and scaffoldable.
Twenty composable archetypes cover mainstream information, editing, system, and utility workflows with deterministic scaffolding.
Server state, virtualization, grouping, pagination/infinite loading, filters, selection, bulk actions, and responsive tables are owned; spreadsheet-grade grids are outside Golden scope.
Responsive media states and accessible line/area/bar/stacked-bar/donut/sparkline/progress anatomy cover common product needs; advanced engines remain optional/product-specific.
Provider-neutral runtime and opt-in capability packages cover common device boundaries without burdening minimal generated apps.
Fail-closed auth, authorization, linking, session lock, scope reset, and secure-storage boundaries are strong; provider enrollment and backend security remain product-owned.
Locale/message fallback, Intl formatting, pluralization, sorting, timezone, RTL, and deterministic pseudo locales are root-owned.

Landmarks/headings, semantic controls, focus lifecycle, live feedback, ARIA snapshots, keyboard, zoom, forced colors, RTL, and reduced motion are certified on web; native AT/Dynamic Type remain pending.
Profiles, catalog-backed screen scaffolding, collision rollback, Doctor, architecture checks, and representative generated-app challenges preserve the Golden path.
The concise agent contract, 75-owner catalog, 20-pattern registry, 55 discovery challenges, and actionable AST enforcement make correct ownership readily discoverable.
Structural ownership, negative fixtures, functional browsers, curated visual baselines, semantic snapshots, and performance budgets now form an orthogonal certification stack.

Supported route splitting, bundle analysis, conservative budgets, large-data checks, optional-capability leak checks, and deterministic runtime interactions are enforced; native profiling remains release work.
The unchanged equal-category Prompt 0 methodology now reflects a comprehensive, discoverable, scaffoldable, and certified application foundation with explicit native and product-specific boundaries.
